mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4.5% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected future cash flows for equities and thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-rate periods (t-test p > 0.05), or the discount rate sensitivity (Rank IC) is below 0.05 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, investor risk aversion rises, prompting a flight to quality and a negative short-term discounting effect that depresses S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive during inflation spikes above 2% (t-test p < 0.05), or the inflation premium does not materially widen (Rank IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) accompanied by a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) signals a tight labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and pushes up equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% while UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive during such labor market events (t-test p > 0.05), or the wage growth premium (Rank IC) is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeding 2% of the prior month's value, when accompanied by a rising HOUST (retail sales), indicates robust consumer demand that supports higher corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows by >2% and HOUST increases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative during such demand shocks (t-test p > 0.05), or the demand surprise decays rapidly (Rank IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100, followed by a sustained decline over three months, signals supply-side weakness that reduces corporate cash flow expectations and produces negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 and declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05), or the supply shock reverses (INDPRO recovers) before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months in a context of rising employment (PAYEMS), it indicates a structural weakening of labor market headwinds, which reduces discounting pressure and supports positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 for two consecutive months and PAYEMS increases
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such episodes, or the unemployment rate does not translate into lower discounting (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) over three months suggests banks are accumulating liquidity, lowering policy-sensitive risk premiums and producing positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during such liquidity build-ups (t-test p > 0.05), or the liquidity ratio effect is not detected (Rank IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A one-time spike in GDPC1 (real private consumption) above the prior month's record, without a corresponding rise in HOUST (retail sales), may reflect inventory buildup and weak demand, which temporarily depresses forward equity valuations and produces negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 sets a new monthly high while HOUST does not increase in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite the consumption spike (t-test p < 0.05), or the shock decays within 3 months (Rank IC < 0.1).
